statement:
For subjective judgments (like politeness or
empathy), there is no single right answer, so AI
ratings should be compared to the range of
human views, not one gold standard.

For routine text coding (e.g., applying a set
codebook to interviews), LLMs are now good
enough to replace trained human coders.

Because AI models represent some groups poorly
(e.g., older adults), simulated participants will
do more harm than good for diversity in research.

Within 10 years, most survey experiments in
psychology will be tested on simulated
participants before (or instead of) real ones.

If AI can accurately predict an experiment's
result, running that experiment on humans
adds little new knowledge.
